topic: Common-rank policy-set continuity frontier without complier full support. Observe a binary instrument Z and treatment D=1{U<=p_Z}, with U uniform, 0<p0<p1<1, exclusion and instrument independence; outcomes lie in a fixed ordered K-point alphabet. Impose exactly Marx's existential rank similarity: marginally uniform ranks V0,V1 represent Y0,Y1 and have equal conditional laws given U, with no canonical independent-PIT restriction. For a fixed policy grid containing thresholds below p0 and above p1, prove the sharp joint policy-mean set is the union of at most binomial(2K-2,K-1) common-rank lattice-path allocation polytope images, with one-law constructions and finite failure certificates. Characterize Hausdorff continuity by finite path-survival inclusions and prove a centered local Lipschitz bound; give a legal K=3 KL-contiguous discontinuity and the matching impossibility of globally shrinking honest metric inference. Construct globally honest multinomial outer-set and set-of-sets inversion, then prove projected full-loss active-stratum Gaussian calibration only on certified continuity laws, including specified structural-zero sampling faces. Consumer: Marx's Oregon Health Insurance Experiment extrapolations to discounted Medicaid take-up and expansion to never-treated. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Two fresh presolves derived the common-law path construction, the finite survival criterion, and the observed-law discontinuity. Exact rational checks verified 25 primal allocations, six full-system Farkas exclusions of the separately attainable upper-upper corner, and a common certificate excluding five disappearing paths. The positive-t submodel has d_H(S_s,S_t)=2|s-t| and an explicit folded-normal limit. Stronger pairwise-neighborhood Lipschitzness and path-domain-only bootstrap shortcuts were refuted; global confidence-region inversion remained valid. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that snapping every active diagonal boundary and value-intercept form of the full projected Hausdorff-loss partition consistently recovers the same homogeneous loss germ at every certified continuous multi-path switch, including relative lower-dimensional sampling cells. EARLY KILL TEST: Compile the projected K=3 Hausdorff-loss partition at a continuous internal-face point with a propensity/grid tie and compare the snapped germ against exact rational perturbations on every feasible tangent face; stop or pivot the regular branch if any loss piece is missed, any local intercept is nonzero, or the germ changes within the recovered stratum. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_ranksim_pathset_discontinuity.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Under existential rank similarity with a finite ordered outcome alphabet, what is the sharp joint identified set of policy means on a threshold grid extending below p0 and above p1 when Marx's full-and-closed complier-support condition is removed?

source_refs.claim: Marx states that uniform sharpness of counterfactual-average bounds relies on full complier support; without it, the bounding quantiles require generalization.
source_refs.author: Philip Marx

source_refs.claim: For discrete outcomes, structural IV functions are generally set identified, with identifying power depending on instrument and outcome support.
source_refs.author: Andrew Chesher

open_problems.why_unsolved: Marx's uniformly sharp construction uses full complier support to equate the complier and population quantile-quantile supports and make groupwise extremizers jointly attainable. When outcome atoms lie outside complier support, existential rank similarity supplies no canonical probability-integral-transform coupling, so separately sharp coordinates need not arise from one common law. The first proof step that must change is the passage from marginal extrapolation bounds to a single jointly feasible population construction; targeted searches found no sharp joint policy-grid characterization replacing it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-union characterization of the joint policy-mean set by common-rank lattice-path allocation-polytope images, with a one-law construction for every feasible point and finite dual certificates for excluded joint corners.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from binary-instrument complier information to policy extrapolation and identifies full complier support as the uniform-sharpness boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A binary instrument identifies complier outcome distributions -> policies outside the observed propensity interval require extrapolation -> rank similarity uses distributional information -> removing full complier support leaves joint attainability unresolved

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Marx's quantile-quantile containment and extremal rank-coupling proof, replacing the full-support equality by enumeration of order-preserving common-rank paths and coupled allocation feasibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is Marx's latent-index rank-similarity model precisely at the assumption boundary where his uniformly sharp construction stops.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite categorical-IV compatibility representation and KL-divergence finite-sample confidence inversion, imposing common-rank path constraints and optimizing jointly over policy-grid images.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both settings reduce multinomial observations to finite latent-allocation feasibility; the new feature is the nonconvex union induced by common-rank path compatibility.

open_problems.open_problem: Which observable-law perturbations preserve Hausdorff continuity of the finite-union common-rank policy set when feasible rank paths appear, disappear, or merge?

source_refs.claim: Marx identifies loss of full complier support as a boundary where his jointly attainable uniformly sharp rank-similar bounds no longer apply directly.
source_refs.author: Philip Marx

source_refs.claim: Beresteanu and Molinari obtain Hausdorff-consistent estimation for identification regions representable through Aumann expectations of set-valued random variables.
source_refs.author: Arie Beresteanu and Francesca Molinari

source_refs.claim: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer develop Hausdorff-rate and confidence-region theory for identified sets represented by criterion-function minimizers.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing Hausdorff asymptotics treat Aumann-expectation regions or regular level and minimizer sets. Here the correspondence is a nonconvex finite union with law-dependent component domains: an entire path image can vanish while every multinomial probability varies continuously. Coefficient continuity within surviving polytopes therefore does not control the union. The first new proof step is a necessary-and-sufficient comparison between limiting path images and images of paths surviving along every nearby feasible-law sequence; searches combining rank similarity, Hausdorff continuity, and finite polytope unions found no such frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if finite path-survival inclusion criterion for Hausdorff continuity, a centered local Lipschitz bound at every certified law, and an explicit finite-outcome discontinuity whenever the criterion fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its full-support caveat naturally motivates why stability of policy conclusions becomes a first-class issue when common-rank couplings cease to survive.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Distributional IV information sharpens policy extrapolation -> full support makes extremal counterfactuals jointly attainable -> support loss changes which common-rank paths survive -> policy sets may jump under arbitrarily small observed-law perturbations

method_exemplars.technique: Translate Marx's quantile-quantile containment argument into finite path feasibility and prove inclusions between limiting and nearby path images.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required survival criterion must formalize the same joint-attainability failure caused by loss of full complier support.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply their Hausdorff decomposition and set-valued convergence logic separately to each fixed path image, then add finite path-survival control for the union operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Their target is an entire identification region in Hausdorff loss, while the destination asks exactly when analogous continuity survives a law-dependent nonconvex union.

method_exemplars.technique: On certified continuity strata, derive the directional derivative of the finite max-min Hausdorff-loss map and apply derivative-estimation resampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite unions of polytope images generate max-min and absolute-value maps that are typically directionally but not fully differentiable.

open_problems.open_problem: At every certified-continuous common-rank law, including multi-path switches and relative lower-dimensional multinomial faces with structural zeros, can the complete projected Hausdorff-loss partition be consistently recovered so that its snapped local germ yields valid Gaussian calibration?

source_refs.claim: Fang and Santos show that, with a Gaussian first stage, the ordinary bootstrap is consistent only under full differentiability and provide derivative-based resampling for directionally differentiable maps.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye give uniformly valid bootstrap-calibrated projection intervals for smooth functions in moment-(in)equality models using repeated feasibility checks.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Fan and Park derive asymptotic laws for sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds, document possible failure of the ordinary bootstrap, and use a fewer-than-n bootstrap.
source_refs.author: Yanqin Fan and Sang Soo Park

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fang-Santos requires the correct directional derivative, while calibrated projection theory handles smooth projections of moment-defined parameter sets. Projected Hausdorff loss for a common-rank union is assembled from finitely many optimization pieces whose active diagonal boundaries and affine intercepts change at path switches. Structural-zero sampling faces restrict perturbations to relative tangent cones. Missing one feasible piece or retaining a nonzero local intercept changes the limiting law. The first proof step that changes is therefore derivative evaluation: it must be preceded by consistent recovery of every active zero-intercept homogeneous piece on every feasible tangent face. Targeted searches found generic directional-bootstrap and projection-calibration theory, but no result establishing this recovery for law-dependent finite unions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A relative-tangent theorem proving that a data-driven snapped partition recovers every zero-intercept homogeneous piece of the projected Hausdorff-loss germ, followed by its Gaussian max-min or folded-normal limit and uniformly valid active-stratum calibration on certified-continuity laws.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates nonstandard inference by diagnosing ordinary-bootstrap failure and organizes the remedy around correct recovery of a directional map.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A Gaussian first-stage estimator feeds a nonsmooth functional -> ordinary bootstrap validity fails without full differentiability -> inference requires the correct directional map -> common-rank policy sets require recovering that map across active paths and sampling faces

method_exemplars.technique: Prove Hadamard directional differentiability relative to each multinomial tangent cone, consistently estimate the piecewise-homogeneous derivative, and resample the estimated derivative evaluated at Gaussian first-stage draws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired limit is a nonlinear directional functional of multinomial Gaussian noise, but its complete local partition must first be recovered.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt repeated finite-feasibility calibration and active-inequality selection to projected policy coordinates, including path identity in the feasibility program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination also projects a high-dimensional partially identified allocation set, but adds multiple nonconvex path components and structural-zero faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their explicit analysis of nonsmooth sharp-bound limits and bootstrap failure as a calibration benchmark for the proposed derivative-based active-stratum procedure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both settings estimate sharp causal regions formed by extrema over couplings and become non-Gaussian when the active optimizer changes.

open_problems.open_problem: Can globally honest inference for the common-rank policy set remain uniformly informative over multinomial laws containing path-drop discontinuities, or must every uniformly valid Hausdorff confidence procedure fail to shrink along some contiguous sequence?

source_refs.claim: Romano and Shaikh construct confidence regions covering an entire identified set and provide conditions for uniform rather than merely pointwise asymptotic validity.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano and Azeem M. Shaikh

source_refs.claim: Uniform validity is crucial in moment-inequality models because pointwise limit distributions can be discontinuous in the data-generating law.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Patrik Guggenberger

source_refs.claim: Marx's Oregon application extrapolates from lottery compliers to discounted coverage and broader Medicaid expansions, with uniform sharpness under rank similarity relying on full complier support.
source_refs.author: Philip Marx

open_problems.why_unsolved: General identified-set and moment-inequality methods provide routes to uniform coverage, but do not settle informativeness when the causal identified-set correspondence itself is discontinuous. At a common-rank path-drop law, multinomial experiments may be statistically contiguous while their sharp policy sets remain a fixed Hausdorff distance apart, obstructing procedures that are both globally honest and uniformly shrinking. The positive construction must therefore invert an observed-law confidence region into an outer policy set or a set of admissible sharp sets rather than rely on a globally regular plug-in map. Searches found no impossibility-and-inversion pair specialized to rank-similar policy extrapolation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A contiguous finite-alphabet submodel proving a nonvanishing lower bound on the diameter of every globally honest Hausdorff confidence region, paired with a finite-sample-valid multinomial inversion procedure covering the sharp policy set or the corresponding set of admissible sets.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates inference on points from coverage of the entire identified set and motivates uniformity through nearby data-generating processes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial identification makes the set itself the target -> pointwise coverage can fail along nearby laws -> uniform set coverage is the relevant guarantee -> discontinuous rank-policy correspondences force a tradeoff between honesty and shrinking diameter

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt familywise test inversion over latent-allocation feasibility without requiring a consistent preliminary estimator of the discontinuous sharp set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The positive target is uniform coverage of an entire partially identified causal set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use contiguous sequences crossing binding-inequality regimes for the impossibility argument, reserving plug-in or subsampling critical values for outer feasibility tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Their analysis isolates discontinuous pointwise asymptotics as the reason uniform procedures require different calibration.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their KL-divergence tail bound for multinomial categorical-IV cells to form a finite-sample observed-law confidence region, then map every admitted law through rank-path feasibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a directly compatible multinomial outer-law device without differentiability of the sharp-set correspondence.

literature_map:
Heckman and Vytlacil (2005, Econometrica) make the MTE the policy-invariant object connecting latent-index selection to counterfactual policy evaluation.
Imbens and Rubin (1997, Review of Economic Studies) show that binary-IV assumptions identify complete marginal outcome distributions for compliers, not only their mean LATE.
Chernozhukov and Hansen (2005, Econometrica) formulate IV quantile treatment effects through restrictions on latent ranks across treatment states.
Chesher (2010, Econometrica) shows why discrete outcomes generally turn structural-IV recovery into set identification and why support determines identifying power.
Brinch, Mogstad, and Wiswall (2017, Journal of Political Economy) identify MTEs from a discrete instrument by functional-form restrictions, providing the linear-extrapolation comparator.
Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018, Econometrica) formulate policy-relevant IV extrapolation through restrictions on weighted averages of a common MTE function.
Mogstad and Torgovitsky (2018, Annual Review of Economics) emphasize that policy populations generally differ from instrument-induced compliers, making extrapolation unavoidable.
Marx (2024, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2012.02390) exploits identified outcome distributions and stochastic orders, applies rank similarity to Oregon Medicaid, and explicitly states that uniform sharpness relies on full complier support.
Kowalski's Oregon analysis and Marx's rank-similar analysis illustrate substantively different extrapolations for Medicaid expansion to the never-treated.
Firpo and Ridder (2019, Journal of Econometrics) distinguish pointwise from uniform sharpness for treatment-effect-distribution bounds, reinforcing the joint-attainability issue.
Beresteanu and Molinari (2008, Econometrica) establish Hausdorff asymptotics for Aumann-expectation identification regions; the common-rank target instead has law-dependent nonconvex-union components.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) and Romano and Shaikh (2010), both Econometrica, provide criterion-based and uniformly valid confidence regions for identified sets.
Andrews and Guggenberger (2009, Econometric Theory) show why discontinuous pointwise asymptotics make uniform validity essential in moment-inequality problems.
Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica) calibrate uniformly valid projection intervals through repeated feasibility checks, but their target is a smooth projection rather than a path-switching union.
Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies), Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory), and Song et al. (2024, arXiv:2405.09510) supply directional-bootstrap theory, nonsmooth sharp-bound inference, and finite categorical-IV KL inversion, respectively.
